I know a lot of people absolutely love A Quiet Place. I wanted to. I really did. Especially because I genuinely like the actors involved. But for me, this film was mostly just boring. The central concept is interesting. A world where making noise can get you killed should create enormous tension. Every movement matters. Every sound matters. Even basic everyday actions suddenly become dangerous. On paper, that is a fantastic horror premise. In practice, I spent a lot of the film waiting for something to happen. And not in the good, tension building way. Just waiting. The movie relies heavily on silence and restraint, but for me that restraint never transformed into enough suspense to justify how little actually happens. That is especially frustrating because I can see why the concept works for other people. The silence creates vulnerability. The limited communication creates tension. The threat is constantly present. I understand all of that. It just never grabbed me emotionally. There were also far too many questions left unanswered for my taste. I do not need a horror film to explain every detail of its world, but I do need enough information to feel like the rules and the setting are more than just a convenient framework for suspense. Here, too much remained vague. That made the world feel less fascinating rather than more mysterious. The performances are good. The concept is good. The execution simply does not work for me. And that is probably the most disappointing kind of film. Not one where I cannot understand the appeal. One where I understand it perfectly and still feel absolutely nothing. A clever horror concept with strong actors that somehow left me more bored than tense, with too little happening and too much left unexplained.

You don't need a railgun; you apparently just need a loud speaker playing feedback. Third, who walks through a hyper-dangerous acoustic wasteland and puts their kids, especially the youngest, most unpredictable one, all the way at the back of the line where nobody can see him? Dumb writers, amazing concept. 2 stars for execution.

The movie is impressively executed, but not as fun as one would like, because every scene is so stressful. It's just not possible to be quiet all the time. You know, a baby that cries all the time and has no control over the noises they make. A Quiet Place has such a strong premise and there are definitely moments where the tension works really well, but I don’t think I connected with it as much as I expected to. John Krasinski and Emily Blunt are both really, really good throughout. Their performances do a lot of the heavy lifting because so much of the film relies on looks, body language and small reactions rather than dialogue. The family dynamic feels believable, and there’s enough emotion underneath everything to make the quieter moments work. I just struggled with how little actual dialogue there is. I understand that’s obviously the entire concept of the film, but there were definitely points where I found myself skipping forward 10 seconds here and there because the silence started to drag for me. It wasn’t necessarily boring, because there is always tension underneath it, but it did make parts of the film feel slower than they probably were. The sign language was also a problem for me because the version I watched didn’t actually give me subtitles for most of it, so there were quite a few conversations where I was basically just guessing what was being said. That obviously isn’t really the film’s fault, but it definitely affected my experience watching it. There are some really effective sequences though. The sound design is clever, the creatures are intimidating, and I liked how vulnerable the family always feels because one tiny mistake can basically get them killed. Krasinski sacrificing himself towards the end also genuinely got to me. I didn’t expect that moment to make me as sad as it did, but it works because the relationship between him and his kids has been built up so quietly throughout the film. I can completely understand why people love this, and I do think it’s a good film. I just don’t think the silent format fully worked for me personally. There were moments where I was really engaged, but there were also moments where I was just waiting for something to happen. Good premise, strong performances, great tension in places, but not one I connected with as much as I hoped.

Dystopia as a genre acts as a medium to warn the audience of a potential future. It comes as a warning as to what might happen if we don't change. Apocalypse is the ashes of dystopia and (in at least my mind) piggybacks off of similar concepts. In order for apocalypse to work it has to have rhyme, reason and a message. There must be cause and reason to our suffering. In AQP there is no cause. And there is so reason. All I gained from the ending was the empty feeling that I should've just doomscrolled tumblr instead and we are never once made aware of the causes of this apocalypse. While supernatural and monsterish apocalypse can exist they typically only work when tied to preexisting beliefs or a sublime divinity (like the 7 trumpets or mayan calender of 2012) so when a random out-of-the-blue unexplained creature shows up I simply do not care. What works in the apocalypse of movies like the 28 series is the undeniable humanity and plausibility of how it happened and what follows it. The first of the series haunts me because of the actions of humanity which I can frankly see people enacting but that terror of possibility is not present in this film. When I look at other apocalypse films I see warning and I see dread for the future. When I look at this I see a pathetic wet dream and a longing to be good. And I'll throw it a bone. It isn't good.
